name: Barzillai
overview: Barzillai is a male figure mentioned in Scripture, known primarily as a man who took a wife from the daughters of Barzillai and was called by their name. There is no recorded tribal affiliation or additional notes about him in the biblical text. His identity is preserved through this unique familial connection.
namesAndTitles: The name Barzillai means '[made of] iron,' indicating strength or resilience. This is a proper name and was not given directly by God. The meaning highlights a characteristic that may reflect the nature or reputation of those bearing the name.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for this person beyond what is listed in the unique attribute, namely his marriage to a daughter of Barzillai. No further familial ties or relationships are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Barzillai's significance in the biblical narrative lies in his connection through marriage to the daughters of another Barzillai, which led to him being called by their name. This detail underscores the importance of family and tribal identity in Israel's history, as well as the transmission of names and heritage. His mention, though brief, contributes to the genealogical and relational records preserved in Scripture.
